name: Orforglipron

b.x: Orforglipron (Foundayo, CAS 2212020-52-3, molecular formula C48H48F2N10O5, MW 883 Da) is a synthetic small molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist, not a peptide. Eli Lilly developed it as LY3502970, a compound also coded OWL833 [6]. It's the first oral GLP-1 drug that requires no fasting window and no absorption enhancer. The drug binds within the transmembrane core of the GLP-1 receptor at a different site than semaglutide or native GLP-1. This allosteric mechanism triggers the same downstream cascade: insulin secretion, glucagon suppression, delayed gastric emptying, and appetite reduction through hypothalamic signaling. Oral bioavailability is 77% on the FDA label, and there are zero fasting or water restrictions. Take it any time of day with or without food. In ATTAIN-1 (n=3,127, 72 weeks) [1], the top dose cut body weight by 11.2%, vs 2.1% on placebo. That dose was 36 mg in the trial and is sold as Foundayo 17.2 mg. People who stayed on treatment lost 12.4%. In ACHIEVE-3 [4], orforglipron 36 mg lowered HbA1c more than oral semaglutide 14 mg (1.91 vs 1.47 points at 52 weeks). In ATTAIN-MAINTAIN [5], people switched from injectable tirzepatide or semaglutide kept 75 to 79% of their weight loss at 52 weeks. On placebo they kept 38 to 49%. The FDA approved Foundayo on April 1, 2026 for chronic weight management in adults with obesity (BMI 30+) or overweight (BMI 27+) with at least one weight-related comorbidity. In ACHIEVE-3, 9 to 10% stopped orforglipron for side effects, vs 4 to 5% on oral semaglutide. Cardiovascular data now exist for type 2 diabetes. ACHIEVE-4 (n=2,749, Lancet 2026) [3] found major cardiovascular events in 4.2% on orforglipron vs 5.0% on insulin glargine over a median 2 years. That met non-inferiority (HR 0.84), which shows heart safety, not a proven heart benefit. The drug launched in April 2026, and this page has not yet summarized community reports.

Most GLP-1 drugs are peptides that mimic the gut hormone GLP-1 by binding to the same pocket on the receptor's surface. Orforglipron does something different. At 883 daltons, it's a fraction of the size of semaglutide (4,114 Da) and binds inside the receptor's transmembrane domain rather than the extracellular orthosteric pocket. Specifically, it contacts transmembrane helices 1, 2, 3, and 7 along with extracellular loop 2 (ECL2). This allosteric binding stabilizes the receptor in an active conformation that preferentially activates Gs-protein signaling. The downstream result is identical to what injectable GLP-1 drugs produce: glucose-dependent insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells, glucagon suppression from alpha cells, slowed gastric emptying, and reduced appetite via hypothalamic and brainstem GLP-1 receptors. The small-molecule scaffold makes orforglipron resistant to proteolytic degradation in the GI tract. Stomach acid and digestive enzymes break down peptide-based GLP-1 agonists within minutes; orforglipron passes through intact. Oral bioavailability is 77% on the FDA label, without any absorption enhancers or food restrictions. Hepatic CYP3A4 handles primary metabolism. The label puts the half-life at about 29 to 49 hours. A Phase 1a study measured 25 to 68 hours, depending on dose and treatment duration (Pratt et al.) [2]. Either way, once-daily dosing works. Peak plasma concentration arrives 4 to 8 hours after swallowing the tablet.
Orforglipron benefits center on accessible GLP-1 therapy without injections or complicated dosing rules.
11.2% average body weight loss at 72 weeks on the highest dose in ATTAIN-1 (3,127 adults) [1]. Those who stayed on treatment lost 12.4%. Overall, 54.6% lost 10% or more.
No food, water, or fasting rules. Oral semaglutide (Rybelsus) must be taken on an empty stomach with up to 4 oz of water, then 30 minutes before eating.
Lowered HbA1c more than oral semaglutide 14 mg head-to-head in ACHIEVE-3 (1.91 vs 1.47 points at 52 weeks) [4].
Triglycerides, non-HDL cholesterol, systolic blood pressure, and waist circumference all improved across ATTAIN-1 dose groups.
People switched from injectable tirzepatide or semaglutide kept 75 to 79% of their weight loss at 52 weeks (ATTAIN-MAINTAIN) [5]. Placebo kept 38 to 49%.

Oral tablet. No vials, no syringes, no reconstitution math. That alone makes orforglipron the simplest GLP-1 drug to start. Titration schedule matters more than most beginners realize. You start at 0.8 mg daily for a full 30 days before moving to 2.5 mg. Then 5.5 mg for another 30 days. After that, you can escalate to 9 mg, 14.5 mg, or 17.2 mg based on how your body responds. Skipping steps or rushing the schedule significantly increases nausea and GI side effects. The detail that catches people off guard: if you miss 7 or more consecutive doses, you restart the entire titration from 0.8 mg. Not from where you left off. Swallow the tablet whole. Don't crush, break, or chew it. Take it any time of day, food or no food, water or no water. No awkward 30-minute fasting window like Rybelsus. Constipation hits harder than most expect (20 to 27% across doses in the label's weight trials, vs 9% on placebo). Start extra fiber and fluids on day 1, not after symptoms appear. Each dose escalation step tends to bring a fresh wave of nausea for 5 to 7 days; plan increases during low-stress weeks.
Cycling Protocol
Intended for continuous long-term use. Weight regain expected after stopping: same as other GLP-1 drugs. If you miss 7 or more consecutive days, restart the titration schedule.

The black box warning comes first. It's the GLP-1 class warning for thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), which other GLP-1 drugs caused in rats and mice. Orforglipron isn't active at the rodent GLP-1 receptor and caused no tumors in rodent studies, so its human risk is unknown (FDA label). Anyone with a personal or family history of MTC or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN2) should not take this drug. Pancreatitis is the second concern. In the two weight trials behind the label, 6 people on orforglipron had confirmed acute pancreatitis, vs 1 on placebo. Severe, persistent abdominal pain radiating to the back warrants immediate medical evaluation and discontinuation. GI side effects are the daily reality for most users during dose escalation. In those trials, nausea hit 26 to 35% across doses (10% on placebo). Constipation ran 20 to 27%, diarrhea 21 to 25%, vomiting 13 to 24%, and dyspepsia 12 to 16%. Abdominal pain, burping, heartburn, and gas round out the GI profile. GI side effects made 3 to 6% stop treatment, vs 0.7% on placebo. In the ACHIEVE-3 comparison, 9 to 10% stopped orforglipron for any side effect, vs 4 to 5% on oral semaglutide [4]. Headache, fatigue, and hair loss appear in the trial data. Heart rate rose 4 to 5 bpm on average in the label's trials (0.5 bpm on placebo). In ACHIEVE-3, pulse rose more on orforglipron than on oral semaglutide (3.7 to 4.7 vs 1.0 to 1.5 bpm). Resting heart rate should be checked at baseline and at each dose escalation. Acute kidney injury is possible during severe GI episodes. Dehydration from vomiting or diarrhea can drop renal perfusion quickly. Renal function monitoring during GI-heavy titration steps is recommended. Gallbladder disease (cholelithiasis, cholecystitis) carries the same class-level association seen with other GLP-1 drugs. Oral hormonal contraceptives may lose effectiveness during initiation and each dose escalation. Gastric emptying delay alters absorption timing. The label recommends switching to a non-oral contraceptive method or adding barrier contraception for 30 days after starting and after each dose increase. Stop orforglipron and contact a provider if you notice a neck mass, persistent hoarseness, difficulty swallowing, severe abdominal pain that doesn't resolve, or signs of a serious allergic reaction. Pregnancy isn't a listed contraindication, but the label says to stop Foundayo once pregnancy is recognized, since weight loss offers no benefit in pregnancy. Women of reproductive potential should use reliable contraception during treatment.
Common Issues & Solutions
Nausea peaks at each dose escalation step: plan dose increases for low-stress weeks; eat smaller, bland meals during the first 5–7 days of each new dose
If GI side effects are severe at a given step, hold at the current dose for 2–4 extra weeks before escalating rather than stopping the drug
Missed ≥7 consecutive doses: restart titration from 0.8 mg: skipping the restart significantly increases GI AE risk at the higher dose
Oral contraceptive users: switch to non-oral formulation before starting; if staying oral, add barrier contraception for 30 days after each escalation step
Constipation (20 to 27% in the label's trials) is as significant as nausea. Increase fluid intake and dietary fiber proactively from day 1, not after onset

Orforglipron (Foundayo) received FDA approval on April 1, 2026 for chronic weight management in adults with a BMI of 30 or greater, or BMI of 27 or greater with at least one weight-related comorbidity. It was the fifth drug approved under the FDA's National Priority Voucher program. Orforglipron is not approved for blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes in the United States, though the Phase 3 ACHIEVE trials tested that use. In the UK, the MHRA authorized Foundayo on August 10, 2026 for weight management and for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes (MHRA press release on GOV.UK). It was the first authorization of orforglipron in Europe. Orforglipron is a patented small molecule manufactured exclusively by Eli Lilly. No generic versions exist. It is not on the FDA drug shortage list, so compounded copies of Foundayo are not permitted. Any product sold as "compounded orforglipron" is fraudulent. Obtain it only through licensed US pharmacies, LillyDirect, or verified telehealth platforms. WADA status has not been determined for orforglipron specifically, though GLP-1 receptor agonists are not currently prohibited in competition. faqs.a: Orforglipron is an oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist from Eli Lilly. Unlike semaglutide (Rybelsus), which is a modified peptide requiring absorption enhancers, orforglipron is a small molecule that can be taken as a simple daily pill. The FDA approved it on April 1, 2026, based on Phase 3 data.

faqs.q: How much weight loss does orforglipron produce?
faqs.a: In ATTAIN-1 (3,127 adults without diabetes), the top dose (17.2 mg Foundayo) cut body weight by 11.2% at 72 weeks, vs 2.1% on placebo. Adults with type 2 diabetes lost 9.6% vs 2.5% in ATTAIN-2. That falls below injectable semaglutide (14.9% in STEP 1) and tirzepatide (20.9% in SURMOUNT-1), but the oral convenience factor drives strong patient interest. Higher doses brought more weight loss and more GI side effects.

faqs.q: What are the side effects of orforglipron?
faqs.a: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation are the most common, consistent with the GLP-1 class. In the two weight trials on the FDA label, 3 to 6% stopped for GI side effects (0.7% on placebo). For any side effect, 6 to 10% stopped. The oral format avoids injection site reactions entirely. Long-term safety data is still accumulating post-approval.

faqs.q: How does orforglipron differ from oral semaglutide (Rybelsus)?
faqs.a: Rybelsus must be taken on an empty stomach with up to 4 oz of water, 30 minutes before food, and uses an absorption enhancer (SNAC). Orforglipron is a small molecule with no food timing restrictions. The FDA label puts its half-life at about 29 to 49 hours, which supports once-daily dosing without the absorption constraints.

faqs.q: What is the recommended Orforglipron dosage?
faqs.a: Orforglipron dosing varies by experience level. Beginners typically start at 0.8 mg daily, moderate users at 5.5 mg daily, and aggressive protocols use 17.2 mg daily.

faqs.q: Does Orforglipron need to be reconstituted?
faqs.a: No. Orforglipron is taken by mouth and is not reconstituted with bacteriostatic water.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of Orforglipron?
faqs.a: The half-life of Orforglipron is ~29-49 hours. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.

summary: FDA approval came 50 days after Eli Lilly filed the application. That speed tells you something about the demand for a GLP-1 drug you can swallow. Orforglipron (brand name Foundayo) is the first oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist to reach the market. It isn't actually a peptide; it's a small molecule that survives stomach acid on its own, no enteric coating or fasting window required. In the ATTAIN-1 trial of 3,127 adults, the highest dose cut body weight by 11.2% at 72 weeks (12.4% among those who stayed on it).
